title: An integral surjective cover of an affine scheme on whose closed subschemes constant cohomology vanishes (Stacks 09ZD (1))
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Then there exists a morphism of schemes $\pi:X'\to X$ which is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that for every closed subscheme $Z'\subseteq X'$ (a closed immersion $Z'\to X'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]), every finite abelian group $M$, with constant sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $Z'_{\Et}$, and every integer $q\ge1$, the etale cohomology group [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] $H^q(Z'_{\Et},\underline M)$ is zero. (Stacks' construction: write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=\mathbf Z[x_i]_{i}/J$, let $R$ be the integral closure of $\mathbf Z[x_i]$ in an algebraic closure of its fraction field and $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(R/JR)$.)

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), part (1), etale-cohomology.tex line 14467; proof, first paragraph (construction via the integral closure R of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and Lemma 09ZC, label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed, line 14445, applied to the normal integral affine scheme Spec R with separably closed function field and its closed subschemes)

proof.text: *Presentation and construction (Stacks: 'Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. Write $A=\mathbf Z[x_i]/J$ ... Let $R$ be the integral closure ... Let $A'=R/JR$ and set $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(A')$').* As $X$ is affine, $X\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; we replace $X$ by $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $P=\mathbf Z[x_a]_{a\in A}$ be the polynomial ring with one variable for each element of $A$; the ring map $P\to A$, $x_a\mapsto a$, is surjective, and with $J$ its kernel we get $A\cong P/J$. $P$ is an integral domain [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]; let $K$ be its field of fractions and $L$ an algebraic closure of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $R\subseteq L$ be the integral closure of $P$ in $L$; by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] (applicable since $L/K$ is algebraic) $R$ is a subring of $L$ containing $P$, integral over $P$. Put $A'=R/JR$ and $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$, and let $\varphi:A=P/J\to R/JR$ be the ring map induced by $P\subseteq R$ (well defined since $J\subseteq JR$); let $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:X'\to X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), line 14467, proof, first paragraph

proof.text: *$\pi$ is integral (left implicit in Stacks).* Every element of $R/JR$ is the class $\bar r$ of some $r\in R$. As $r$ is integral over $P$ there are $p_0,\dots,p_{n-1}\in P$ with $r^n+p_{n-1}r^{n-1}+\dots+p_0=0$ in $R$; reducing modulo $JR$ gives $\bar r^n+\varphi(\bar p_{n-1})\bar r^{n-1}+\dots+\varphi(\bar p_0)=0$, with $\bar p_k$ the class of $p_k$ in $A=P/J$. So $\varphi$ is integral, and $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is an integral morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-integral-ring-map-integral] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), line 14467, proof, first paragraph ('This gives an example as in (1)': integrality of X'->X); literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex Lemma 02K8

proof.text: *$\pi$ is surjective (left implicit in Stacks; lying over, Stacks 00GQ).* The points of $X=\operatorname{Spec}(P/J)$ are the primes $\mathfrak p/J$ with $\mathfrak p\subseteq P$ a prime containing $J$, and $\pi$ sends a prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $R/JR$ to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The inclusion $P\subseteq R$ is injective and integral, so by lying over [pqf-lem-lying-over] there is a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq R$ with $\mathfrak q\cap P=\mathfrak p$. Then $JR\subseteq\mathfrak pR\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak q/JR$ is a prime of $R/JR$, and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=(\mathfrak q\cap P)/J=\mathfrak p/J$. Hence $\pi$ is surjective on underlying sets, i.e. surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 00GQ (label lemma-integral-overring-surjective), line 7735; used for literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), line 14467, proof, first paragraph

proof.text: *$R$ is a normal domain with separably closed fraction field.* By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] $R$ is an integral domain, $L$ is its field of fractions, and $R$ is integrally closed in $L$, i.e. $R$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. $L$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so every nonconstant polynomial over $L$, in particular every nonconstant separable one, has a root in $L$: $L$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a normal integral affine scheme with separably closed function field, the hypothesis of Stacks 09ZC.

source.place: Lemma 09ZD (label lemma-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology), line 14467, proof, first paragraph (hypotheses of Lemma 09ZC, line 14445, for X=Spec R)

proof.text: *Vanishing on closed subschemes of $X'$ (Stacks: 'This gives an example as in (1) by Lemma 09ZC').* Let $Z'\to X'$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $M$ a finite abelian group and $q\ge1$. The morphism $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(R/JR)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ induced by $R\to R/JR$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], so the composite $Z'\to X'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], i.e. $Z'$ is a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. By step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-absolutely-algebraically-closed] (Stacks 09ZC; its proof uses 09Z9 = [sbc-lem-etale-over-normal], Algebra 05WS, 09ZB, which uses 03AJ, 03RV and 09ZA, which uses Algebra 04D1 and 09Z9, and the criterion 0GY0, which uses 09AX) we get $H^q(Z'_{\Et},\underline M)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. With steps 2 and 3, $\pi:X'\to X$ is integral, surjective, and has the required property.

split_report.summary: Split along the first paragraph of Stacks 09ZD's proof: (1) presentation A=Z[x_a]/J and construction of R (integral closure of Z[x_a] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field) and X'=Spec(R/JR); (2) integrality of A->R/JR written out directly (reduce the monic equation mod JR) plus Spec of an integral ring map is integral (new leaf, IsIntegralHom.SpecMap_iff); (3) surjectivity directly by lying over (existing pqf-lem-lying-over, Stacks 00GQ) instead of a base change argument, since primes of P/J are primes of P containing J; (4) R normal domain with algebraically (so separably) closed fraction field (new leaf from Mathlib's integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_algebraic and IsIntegrallyClosedIn instance); (5) a closed subscheme of X' is one of Spec R (spec-quotient closed immersion and new leaf for composition, 01QS), then Stacks 09ZC (new unsplit node). The brief's description of 09ZC was inexact: 09ZC is stated directly for any normal integral affine scheme with separably closed function field (no limit over finite sets of variables, no Noetherian hypothesis); 0GY0 is Gabber's H^1 criterion for rings with strictly henselian local rings, not a limit lemma. The statement is kept.
